tldr: DeepSeek was spotted testing an agent harness in early August, alongside the cheap V4 model that had already jolted Silicon Valley on price. Ten days later it open sourced that harness outright, pairing the release with a pricier V4-Pro API tier.
whats_new: DeepSeek open sourced Harness, a plugin-architecture agent framework pitched as a rival to Claude Code, and paired the launch with V4-Pro API access at higher prices than the base V4 model.
why_it_matters: An open, inspectable agent harness from a low-cost model lab gives platform engineers a second reference architecture to compare against Claude Code, but the accompanying V4-Pro price increase changes the cost math that made DeepSeek attractive in the first place.

beats.headline: DeepSeek spotted testing an agent harness alongside cheap V4
beats.summary: First sign of the harness surfaced while V4's low pricing was already pressuring Silicon Valley labs.

beats.headline: Harness ships open source as a Claude Code rival, with V4-Pro pricier on API
beats.summary: DeepSeek formalized the release as a plugin-based framework and raised API pricing for the paired V4-Pro model.

open_questions: Does Harness's plugin interface match or diverge from Claude Code's tool-calling conventions, and how much rework would porting an existing agent take?
How does V4-Pro's higher API price compare on a cost-per-task basis against base V4 and against Claude Code once agent overhead is factored in?
Will independent benchmarks test Harness's plugin architecture against established agent frameworks, or is this still framework-only with no eval data?
take_for_builders: Before treating DeepSeek Harness as a Claude Code substitute, check whether its plugin interface covers your current tool-calling and memory setup, and re-run your cost comparison against V4-Pro's new, higher API price.
